summary: This sermon calls Christians to resist cultural isolation and digital tribalism by prioritizing embodied, face-to-face community centered around the communion table. The pastor argues that while humans were created for intimate community in God's image, sin and modern culture—especially social media and the idealization of the nuclear family—have pulled us out of tune with that design, requiring intentional small-group relationships anchored in Christ's broken body and shed blood.
key_points: We over-invest in digital relationships with strangers while neglecting embodied community
Political forces have discipled us to dehumanize those we disagree with
God created humanity for community, imaging the relational Trinity
Modern obstacles like social media and nuclear-family idealization isolate us from biblical community
Jesus modeled investing in different sized communities and invites us to the communion table
big_idea: Christians must resist cultural isolation by intentionally gathering in small, embodied communities centered on Christ's broken body and shed blood at the communion table.
title: PTW COMMUNITY: Be Family Around a Table
